risk_if_not_implemented: Without Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Supply Chain Visibility, sensitive data with long confidentiality lifetimes remains protected only by quantum-vulnerable cryptography, exposing it to future decryption. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Uncontrolled Third-Party Security / Privacy Exposure (R-GV-5), Lack of oversight of third-party controls (R-GV-7), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Cryptographic Compromise / Cryptanalytic Capability Advancement (MT-31).

compensating_control_1.name: Review of Third-Party Services
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to monitor, regularly review and assess External Service Providers (ESPs) for compliance with established contractual requirements for security, compliance and resilience controls.
compensating_control_1.justification: Review of Third-Party Services (TPM-15) provides periodic assessment and verification that compensates for the absence of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Supply Chain Visibility (QTS-06.3) by providing structured evaluation of the environment to surface gaps and verify residual control effectiveness. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Third-Party Contract Requirements
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to require contractual requirements for applicable security, compliance and resilience requirements with third-parties, reflecting the organization's needs to protect its Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).
compensating_control_2.justification: Third-Party Contract Requirements (TPM-14) provides third-party oversight and contractual controls that compensates for the absence of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Supply Chain Visibility (QTS-06.3) by extending security obligations and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct primary control implementation. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
